description: A single-panel figure that is a two-column data table rendered as an image — no axes, no plot, no scale bar, no micrograph. The left column is headed "possible (κ-) carbides structure" and the right column "Formation energy (eV/atom)"; the image itself contains no caption text. Four rows are printed: the κ-carbides entry "(Fe, Mn)3AlC" with formation energy −0.160; the "Cr-rich carbides" entry "Cr21(FeC3)2" with −0.049; the "Ni-rich carbides" entry "Fe2NiC" with 0.082; and a final entry "AlNi3C" with −0.181 whose left-hand group cell is blank. Ordered by magnitude, AlNi3C is the most negative (−0.181), then the κ-carbide (Fe, Mn)3AlC (−0.160), then Cr21(FeC3)2 (−0.049); Fe2NiC is the only structure with a positive value, i.e. the only one unfavourable relative to its reference state. The three negative formation energies are the figure's evidence that κ-carbide-type and Cr-rich carbides are energetically favourable to form, with (Fe, Mn)3AlC close to the most stable option listed. No computational parameters (functional, cutoff, k-points) appear in the figure.

observations.observation: The figure is a single two-column table; the column headers read exactly "possible (κ-) carbides structure" and "Formation energy (eV/atom)".
The row labelled κ-carbides lists the structure "(Fe, Mn)3AlC" with formation energy −0.160 eV/atom.
The row labelled Cr-rich carbides lists the structure "Cr21(FeC3)2" with formation energy −0.049 eV/atom.
The row labelled Ni-rich carbides lists the structure "Fe2NiC" with formation energy 0.082 eV/atom.
A fourth entry, "AlNi3C", is printed with formation energy −0.181 eV/atom, and its left-column group label is blank.
Fe2NiC is the only structure in the table with a positive formation energy (0.082 eV/atom); the other three values are negative.
Among the printed values, AlNi3C (−0.181) is the most negative, followed by the κ-carbide (Fe, Mn)3AlC (−0.160), then Cr21(FeC3)2 (−0.049).
The caption states the table gives first-principle calculation results of formation energy for the possible κ-carbides structure formation.

The figure reports no computational details (exchange-correlation functional, plane-wave cutoff, k-point sampling) and no temperature or pressure conditions — the image does not confirm the calculation setup.

subfigures.description: One two-column table of first-principles formation energies: header row "possible (κ-) carbides structure" / "Formation energy (eV/atom)", then rows κ-carbides (Fe, Mn)3AlC −0.160; Cr-rich carbides Cr21(FeC3)2 −0.049; Ni-rich carbides Fe2NiC 0.082; and AlNi3C −0.181 with a blank group label. Values are printed to three decimals.
